chapter: Swing and what makes a band play
title: Latin rhythm, George Benson and the meaning of swing
summary: They debate whether Latin rhythm sections swing; McShann says Latin is structural while swing is free, praising George Benson's flexibility.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, just one thing. When Dizzy gets into his Latin American things, that's a different kind of a thing, like it's a different -- that's got a -- that is swinging, in a way. It's a different kind of a thing. Or would you say not?
Well, here's what that is. That is --
That seems to be the rhythm he likes. That Latin rhythm.
He feels more at home with that Latin
But he's not -- I still say he's not swinging. All right, we'll turn around and get somebody like this kid that did this thing, George Benson.
He play them Latin rhythms and swing. See what I'm talking about, the difference?
He'll play them Latin rhythms and that other stuff --

Now you're talking. You got to be flexible. Some people have to stay -- have to walk the chalk line. Some people don't have to -- they can walk the same distance and don't have to walk the chalk line.
But I mean some of those Latin rhythm sections, they swing all right, in their way, don't they?
You hear some of those groups with congas and just one trumpet, they're swinging.
It's a different thing, but they are.
But when we speak of swing though, I draw the line. What I mean -- see, your Latin is a structural thing.
Swing is not structural. You swing. Either you swing or you don't.
Yeah, that's right. But I will --
But you cannot say that they are not -- follow me close. You're not saying that they're not swinging. Here's what I mean, but in their structural --
They're swinging in a different format.
In a format, and what we're talking about is not a format.

But actually that is the same thing that Jay is talking about. You get those Latin groups with a rhythm section, I would say, is very often swinging. But what those trumpets are doing up there, so that they're kind of
playing figures, but they're not really swinging. They're not bending with it, but the rhythm sections in a lot of Latin groups, I would have thought -- you know?
Yeah, for the structural thing that they are doing, within -- that's, you know, structure. Remember, the -- as you said, you mentioned the trumpets, they're still within the structure, too.
They're still within that same structure.
Swing is free. A lot of people -- blues is free.
